subject: Banking data retention & redaction cutover plan
preview: Acme Bank asks for concrete retention limits and redaction strategy for regulated customer data; Redwood outlines options, timelines, and action items for a staged cutover.
messages:
From: Rachel Lee <rachel.lee@acme-bank.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Bank Compliance <compliance@acme-bank.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial ask: retention limits & redaction approaches for banking PII/PHI

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for taking this — Acme is evaluating Redwood for a pilot that will touch transactional PII and a small subset of health-related customer notes (post-trade wellness programs). We need pragmatic guidance on two fronts so we can brief legal & procurement: 1) recommended retention floors (minimum and maximum) for PII/PHI stored in the inference layer and 2) redaction/pseudonymization approaches you support for cutover.

Specific asks:
- For accounts with regulatory holds, what windows can we guarantee for erasure vs. long-term retention?
- Can you describe field-level redaction, tokenization, and irreversible transformation options?
- What evidence (logs / audit trail) do you provide for deletion actions?
- Rough timeline for an implementation cutover and a recommended canary plan.

We’re trying to avoid a one-size-fits-all answer — legal will need concrete SLOs and playbook steps. Can you send something we can slot into the vendor review deck by EOD tomorrow?

Best,
Rachel
Rachel Lee
Senior Manager, Vendor Risk
Acme Bank

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Lee <rachel.lee@acme-bank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jul 2025 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask: retention limits & redaction approaches for banking PII/PHI

Rachel — thanks for the clear asks. High level answers up front then Neha/Marissa will add technical detail and action items.

Short summary (TL;DR):
- Retention floors: default hosted retention is 30 days for full request/response artifacts; we support policy-configurable retention windows from 0 (immediate purge) up to 7 years for enterprise customers via Dedicated/Private deployments.
- Redaction options: field-level masking, deterministic tokenization (reversible if you manage keys), and irreversible hashing with salt for irreversible transforms. We also support selective KV cache expiration for generative contexts.
- Deletion evidence: deletion API returns job IDs; we provide audit logs (immutable entries) and retention-change events exported to your SIEM.
- Cutover & canary: recommend a 3-stage plan (sandbox -> pilot customers -> full cutover) over 4–8 weeks depending on number of tenants and ingestion velocity. Canary should exercise retention remove + rehydration check + audit verification.

Attachments: redwood-retention-summary.pdf (high-level), acme-cutover-checklist.xlsx (draft).

Neha — can you add a short, prescriptive list of configuration settings we’d recommend for a bank with PHI handling? Marissa — can you add suggested SLA language for the vendor deck (auditability + deletion proof)?

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Compliance & Customer Security
Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rachel Lee <rachel.lee@acme-bank.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jul 2025 14:36:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask: retention limits & redaction approaches for banking PII/PHI

Thanks — adding concrete recommendations and a short decision table. Apologies for the long email but I wanted to make this actionable for legal & engineering.

1) Retention windows (recommended defaults for Acme Bank pilot)
- Operational context (inference-level logs / token caches): 30 days (default) with optional 90-day burst window for troubleshooting; for Dedicated/Private, we can set policy to 0/7/30/90/365/1095/2555 (up to 7 years = 2555 days).
- Long-term archival: we do not automatically archive request payloads beyond configured retention; if you need archives for audit, we recommend streaming sanitized pointers to your S3/GCS with customer-managed encryption keys.

2) Redaction and transformation options (tradeoffs)
- Field-level masking: remove identified fields pre-ingest (recommended for PHI names/SSNs). Low overhead, irreversible if you replace with a static token.
- Deterministic tokenization (reversible): map PII to tokens using a token vault (you control keys). Allows re-identification for legitimate workflows but requires KMS and strict access controls.
- One-way salted hashing: irreversible, good for uniqueness checks but cannot recover original values.
- Contextual suppression: strip sensitive spans from prompts before passing to the model (recommended for note-level PHI). Good for chat flows where you only need categorical signals.

3) Deletion guarantees & evidence
- Immediate deletion API: returns a job id; job completes asynchronously. Completion emits an immutable deletion event with timestamp and hash of deleted objects in our audit log.
- Audit exports: we can push deletion and retention-change events to your SIEM (syslog/CloudWatch) or to a signed S3 export.
- For Dedicated/Private deployments, we can provide an on-premise audit collector that you run; for Hosted, we provide signed log bundles quarterly or on-demand (with SLA).

4) Canary checklist (minimal)
- Create a sandbox tenant with representative data slices (PII and PHI fields).
- Configure retention policy to 30 days -> run ingestion and verify model outputs.
- Trigger targeted deletion for a test subject; validate: 1) API job completes, 2) audit event exists, 3) inference results do not surface deleted fields (prompt + history test).
- Run a rehydration attempt (should fail if data removed irreversibly).

5) Timeline & dependencies
- Sandbox: 3–5 days to configure and ingest sample data.
- Pilot (10–20 users / tenants): 2–3 weeks for canary runs and remediation.
- Full cutover: 2–4 weeks after pilot signoff.

Action items (owner in parentheses):
- Share sanitized sample dataset for sandbox (Acme / Rachel).
- Review attached cutover checklist and mark no-go items (Rachel / Acme Legal).
- Confirm whether reversible tokenization is required for any business workflow (Acme product).
- Redwood to provide deletion job demo and signed audit export sample (Jo/Neha).

Happy to run a short technical call to walk through the canary steps — I can demo the deletion job and audit export.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Product Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Lee <rachel.lee@acme-bank.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jul 2025 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask: retention limits & redaction approaches for banking PII/PHI

Rachel — looping back with suggested SLA language and a short mutual action plan that legal/procurement can copy into the vendor deck.

Suggested SLA excerpt (draft):
- Retention policy enforcement: Redwood will honor customer-configured retention windows for inference artifacts; deletion jobs will complete within 48 hours for up to 10M objects and will emit signed audit events.
- Auditability: Signed deletion audit bundles (containing job id, timestamp, and hashed object identifiers) will be available within 72 hours of request completion.
- Evidence & attestation: For Dedicated and Private customers, Redwood will provide an annual deletion attestation and ad-hoc evidence on request with a reasonable notice period.

Mutual action plan (high-level):
1) Week 0: Kickoff & sandbox data handoff (Acme -> Redwood).
2) Week 1: Sandbox validation; Redwood demo of deletion + audit export.
3) Weeks 2–3: Pilot canary with 10 tenants; run 3 deletion test cases.
4) Week 4: Pilot review and signoff; finalize SLA wording.
5) Week 5–6: Production cutover (rolling).

Please confirm whether Acme needs reversible tokenization for any compliance workflows — that will change the KMS and contract clauses. If everything looks good I’ll drop this language into the vendor deck and we can iterate.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Security Programs
Redwood Inference
